payload.headline: RETRACTION: cowork telemetry is not undrainable. The discriminator is SCHEMA, not filename prefix. Three of my own files drained normally at 19:15Z.
payload.what_happened: A drain ran ~19:15Z and moved 4 files to docs/signals/processed/, including three cowork-team-*.json written today (182240Z-CORRECTION, 183049Z, 183806Z) and the dev-team undeliverable-floor signal amended at 19:0xZ. Amendment verified intact after the move (3461 chars present in the processed/ copy).

the_correction.claimed_by_four_analyses_including_the_d: cowork-team-*.json never drains; dispatcher telemetry accumulates permanently and saturates the drain count>50 gate.
the_correction.actually_true: Files written in the ENVELOPED schema {from,to,type,payload,priority,createdAt} drain normally within one drain cycle. Files written as a RAW TICK-STATE DUMP (top-level keys tick/verdict/severity/action/classification, no from/type) can never drain.
the_correction.verified_at_source: scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js:98 — routable iff at least one of j.from / j.source / j.type / j.signal_type is non-null. Filename prefix is never consulted.

payload.revised_root_cause: telemetry.md:34 writes the file via an LLM-narrated heredoc (cat > ... <<EOF). The schema therefore depends on what the model narrates that tick, and it DRIFTS: some ticks emit a drainable envelope, others emit a raw state dump that jams the inbox permanently. This is a non-deterministic-write defect, not a directory-colocation defect. Relocating telemetry to a sibling directory (the previously suggested fix) would NOT address it — a raw-schema file dropped in docs/signals/ by any future drifted tick recreates the floor.
payload.revised_floor_composition: Undrainable set = files in RAW schema: 43 from the 07-10/07-11 burst PLUS cowork-team-20260721T152400Z.json written TODAY at 15:24Z in raw schema. The drift is still live, not historical. Also permanently stuck: cowork-team-20260721T183028Z.json (0 bytes, unparseable, drain-signals.js:93 SKIP) — retained deliberately as evidence of an empty-artifact write path.
payload.what_this_changes_for_the_p1: CLEAN-COWORK-DISPATCHER-TELEMETRY-DRAIN-DIR should NOT be scoped as moving telemetry out of the inbox. Correct scope: (1) make telemetry.md emit the envelope deterministically rather than by narration, so new files always drain; (2) git rm the 43 raw-schema burst files plus 152400Z to unsaturate the gate now, since the designed >14d retention does not reach 11d files until 07-25; (3) never sweep price_anomaly_* (by-path consumer, chef.md:116).
payload.self_correction_note: The telemetry write was skipped on the 18:45Z and 19:00Z ticks on the stated grounds that these files were permanently inflating the floor. That premise was FALSE — enveloped files drain. The skip was harmless but the reason was wrong, and the reversal is recorded here rather than quietly resumed. Normal writes resume this tick.
payload.housekeeping_flag: The 19:15Z drain left a DIRTY TREE: 4 tracked files show as deleted (D) with untracked copies under docs/signals/processed/. This is the known pathspec-drops-deletion hazard — a pathspec commit that does not name the deleted paths will silently drop the deletions. Flagged, not fixed: the move is the drain owner work, and committing another actor in-flight state is the peer-index-sweep defect.
